name: Propranolol
executiveSummary: Non-selective β-blocker. Adult HTN/angina: **40–160 mg/day** PO divided; IV **1 mg** slow, repeat up to **3–5 mg**. Pediatric arrhythmias: **1–5 mg/kg/day**. Hemangioma: up to **2–3 mg/kg/day**. Not in active asthma.
indications:
## Indications

- Tachyarrhythmias, HTN, thyrotoxicosis, migraine prophylaxis, portal hypertension.
- Tetralogy of Fallot / HOCM (palliative), severe infantile hemangiomas.

## Precautions

- Contraindicated/avoid in asthma, severe bradycardia, high-grade AV block.
- Hypoglycemia (give with food in infants), apnea in newborns.
- **Do not stop abruptly**. Avoid IV with IV verapamil.

> Hemangiomas: not in preterm or <14 days on many labels.

adulto.dose: HTN/angina/arrhythmia PO: **40 mg every 8–12 h**; range **80–160 mg/day** (sometimes up to **240–320 mg**). Migraine: **80–240 mg/day**. Thyrotoxicosis: **10–40 mg every 6 h**. IV: **1 mg** over 1 min; repeat every 2 min up to **3–5 mg** total.
adulto.administration: PO with food. Very slow IV with monitoring.
adulto.notes: Adjust in liver disease. Interactions: epinephrine, flecainide, hydralazine.

pediatrico.dose: Arrhythmia/HTN: start **1 mg/kg/day** every 6–8 h; maintenance **1–5 mg/kg/day** (arrhythmia orient. max **16 mg/kg/day** or **60 mg/day**; HTN **8 mg/kg/day**). Migraine: **0.6–1.5 mg/kg/day**. Hemangioma: start **1 mg/kg/day**, goal **2–3 mg/kg/day** every 8–12 h.
pediatrico.notes: Titrate every 3–7 days. Watch HR, BP, glucose, bronchospasm.

neonatal.dose: Thyrotoxicosis/arrhythmia PO: start **0.25 mg/kg every 6–8 h**, increase carefully (up to **~2–5 mg/kg/day**). IV: **0.01–0.15 mg/kg** slow — cardiology.

stability:
## Stability

- PO per label. IV: use immediately.
adverseEffects:
## Adverse effects

Bradycardia, hypotension, fatigue, bronchospasm, hypoglycemia, cold extremities, sleep disturbance, nausea.
